nodes.title: Where work comes from
nodes.say: Work reaches the agent runtime through a direct A P I call, a hand-off from chat, or a schedule. Choose a source.
nodes.decidedBy: The entry point that admits it: a POST to the V3 tasks API, or a goal trigger the agent runtime stamps with GoalSource (User, Schedule or ChatInline).

options.label: V3 task API
options.say: A client creates a task over HTTP, then calls the execute route to run it.

options.label: Chat delegates to an agent
options.say: A chat turn hands a goal to a named agent, which opens a task-backed run in the caller's scope.

options.label: Chat runs a heavy capability pack
options.say: A chat turn names one pack call with every argument, and it runs inside a real internal task.

options.label: A schedule fires
options.say: A cron trigger comes due, or a sleeping agent's wake-up time arrives, and the scheduler launches a cycle.

nodes.title: Task created, then executed
nodes.say: The task API mints an ID and stores the task record through the reducer; a second call to the execute route asks the service to run it.

nodes.title: Chat delegates a goal
nodes.say: The chat service triggers the agent runtime with a chat-inline goal, which opens a task with an execution shell and spawns a goal cycle job.

nodes.title: Chat runs a pack as a task
nodes.say: Chat builds a pre-decided pack call, creates an internal task with an execution shell, and runs it inline so progress streams into the chat card.

nodes.title: Scheduler tick
nodes.say: Every few seconds a supervisor tick collects due cron triggers per scope and dispatches each within a budget; sleeping agents come back through the wake queue.

nodes.title: Execution launched
nodes.say: The service saves a new execution record and hands the run to a separate execution runtime, so the HTTP worker never runs it.

nodes.title: Agentic executor starts
nodes.say: Every path reaches the orchestrator, which calls the agentic executor. It builds the run setup: resolving the owner, scoping tools and arming the deadline watchdog.

nodes.title: One phase per lease
nodes.say: The stateless driver claims a fenced lease, runs exactly one phase, journals and commits it, then releases the lease or keeps it for the next phase.

nodes.title: Prepare and observe
nodes.say: Prepare hydrates the checkpoint, labels the stream and announces the iteration; Observe then settles what the agent currently knows before anything is decided.

nodes.title: Deciding the next move
nodes.say: Each iteration, the next move can come from a pre-decided call, the decision engine, a pinned harness, or Magician's own model, tried in that order. Pick one to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: Checked in this order in the Decide phase: ctx.predecided_call; then decision_backend_for(run engine), allowed by decision.mode (all_engines, magician_only or off) in magician-config.yaml; then execution.harness_engine (or the run's pin) resolving to TurnEngine::Harness; else the native model.

options.label: Pre-decided pack call
options.say: Checked first: a chat pack that already named its call returns it as is, after the owner's tool policy is projected, so no decider sees the turn.

options.label: Decision engine rail
options.say: Next, when decision mode allows this run's engine, the external decision engine chooses; a transport error fails the turn instead of falling through.

options.label: Pinned harness engine
options.say: Otherwise a harness such as Codex or Claude Code, pinned in settings or by the run, thinks for a whole turn.

options.label: Magician's own model
options.say: Only when nothing above answered does the native decision run, asking Magician's own model for the next tool call, a question or a finish.

nodes.title: Pre-decided call
nodes.say: The pack call chosen in chat becomes this turn's decision, or its settled result becomes the final answer, so the call never fires twice.

nodes.title: Harness takes the turn
nodes.say: A pinned harness runs one bounded Plane turn; its tool calls come back through the same approval and execution path, and it returns a checkpoint, question or yield.

nodes.title: Native model decision
nodes.say: A decision job runs beside the loop: preflight checks first, then a native prompt asks the model for the next tool call, a question or a finish.

nodes.title: Decision resolved
nodes.say: Resolve unwraps the decision, retries a failed one, checks the work budget, and refreshes owner and trust policy before anything acts.

nodes.title: Apply gate
nodes.say: Apply matches on the decision; for an action it checks allowlists, the owner's approval rules and the action's criticality before anything runs.

nodes.title: The approval gate
nodes.say: Before an action touches anything, the gate either lets it through or holds it for a person to approve. Choose which to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: gate_execute: checked_approval against ctx.approval_rules returning ApprovalResult::NeedsApproval, a criticality that requires human confirmation, or the model's own requires_confirmation flag; an action already confirmed skips the gate.

options.label: Allowed
options.say: No approval rule, criticality or model flag asks for confirmation, so the action goes straight to dispatch.

options.label: Needs a human
options.say: A matching approval rule or a critical action pauses the run and asks the owner to confirm first.

nodes.title: Run pauses for approval
nodes.say: The executor saves a full pause state and emits a HitlRequested event, so the web app, desktop and phone all show the same confirmation card.

nodes.title: Owner answers, run resumes
nodes.say: The owner's answer posts to the single HITL respond route; an agentic approval resumes the paused execution with the confirmed action carried in.

nodes.title: Flat tool dispatch
nodes.say: Apply hands the approved action to flat dispatch, which classifies the tool name against the agent's scoped registry, with no inner model involved.

nodes.title: Tool executors
nodes.say: The tool's name decides its executor: a compiled provider, a command-line template, the browser, or a compiled pack. Pick one.
nodes.decidedBy: classify_flat_route: the pack definition's ImplementationType plus the pack__action split of the tool name; the browser pack is special-cased by name.

options.label: Compiled provider primitive
options.say: A pack-and-action call whose pack has a compiled provider, like DuckDB or iMessage, runs one primitive inside Magician.

options.label: CLI template primitive
options.say: A pack-and-action call with no provider, like Gmail or csvkit, runs as a subprocess built from the skill's command template.

options.label: Browser
options.say: A browser action goes to the single-primitive browser dispatcher and this execution's own browser session.

options.label: Plain compiled pack
options.say: A bare tool name like shell or save preference, or a declared compiled leaf, runs through the compiled-pack fast path.

nodes.title: Compiled provider runs
nodes.say: The compiled provider executes the one primitive inside Magician, spend-gated, and its output is folded back into an ordinary action result.

nodes.title: CLI subprocess runs
nodes.say: A scoped invoker loads the skill's command template, resolves the program against the child's own path, and spawns it with a timeout and bounded output.

nodes.title: Compiled pack runs
nodes.say: Flat dispatch injects the runtime's own scope identity, then the compiled-pack fast path runs the handler under the execution's cancel token and sandbox roots.

nodes.title: Epilogue
nodes.say: The epilogue updates the no-action counters, raises a stuck warning after three idle iterations, and emits the iteration-completed event.

nodes.title: Loop or finish
nodes.say: After each iteration the loop either goes round again or finishes with an outcome. Choose which to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: A phase returning PhaseStep::Return with an AgenticOutcome (a yield, failure, cancellation or budget stop) ends the run; otherwise Epilogue has no next phase, so the iteration counter rises against its ceiling and Prepare runs again.

options.label: Finish with an outcome
options.say: The agent yielded its result, or the run failed, was cancelled or ran out of budget, so the loop returns an outcome.

options.label: Another iteration
options.say: Nothing ended the run, so the iteration counter goes up and the driver starts the next Prepare phase.

nodes.title: Quality review
nodes.say: Work can be published straight away, or go through an independent Relentless quality review first. Pick one to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: A Relentless contract on the task: task.manifest.relentless (an owner's TaskRelentlessPolicy, prepared at launch so Relentless owns the run and drives this loop as its actor), or an agent's propose_relentless proposal that the owner approved.

options.label: No contract
options.say: Most tasks carry none, so the outcome is published as soon as the loop finishes.

options.label: Relentless review
options.say: The draft is not trusted on its own word: independent critics score it, and the controller may run the loop again with feedback.

nodes.title: Outcome published
nodes.say: The service saves the final execution outcome, marks synthesis as pending, and spawns the synthesis pipeline that publishes the task's outputs.

nodes.title: Task finished
nodes.say: From an API call, a chat hand-off or a schedule, every phase was committed durably, every action passed the gate, and the outputs are published.

nodes.title: Who asks for review
nodes.say: A review is contracted either by the owner's standing task policy or by the agent itself. Choose one.
nodes.decidedBy: A task-policy launch record written at execution start (read_relentless_launch), versus a durable propose_relentless proposal that the owner approves.

options.label: Owner's task policy
options.say: The owner attached a Relentless policy to the task, so the controller owns the run from launch.

options.label: Agent proposal
options.say: The agent drafted a quality contract with a tool call, and the owner approved it before anything ran.

nodes.title: Policy launch admitted
nodes.say: The service checks the launch identity against the committed task root, admits the run to its store, and starts the controller worker.

nodes.title: Agent proposes review
nodes.say: The propose tool files a durable proposal; once the owner approves, the service binds the run to the task, journals the admission and launches a worker.

nodes.title: Frozen definition of done
nodes.say: The contract freezes into a definition of done: goal, weighted criteria, pinned critic models, sealed sources, a score threshold and a budget.

nodes.title: Controller drives attempts
nodes.say: The controller loops between attempting and reviewing, first quoting the actor plus every critic's retry headroom against the remaining budget.

nodes.title: Actor drafts a candidate
nodes.say: The actor runs the same agentic loop in a sandboxed work area, given the sources, the retained best draft and earlier review feedback.

nodes.title: Independent critics
nodes.say: With the candidate sealed by hash, each pinned critic scores its criteria with confidence and evidence; check criteria run deterministically, with no model.

nodes.title: Verdict validated
nodes.say: Each verdict must match the sealed artifact, contract and evidence; a malformed review goes back to the critic with the validation error.

nodes.title: Panel aggregated
nodes.say: Valid verdicts are combined per criterion, requiring quorum, bounded score spread and must-pass agreement, into one weighted quality score.

nodes.title: The review decision
nodes.say: A deterministic reducer now accepts the draft, sends it back with feedback, stops on a plateau or budget, or waits for the owner. Pick an outcome.
nodes.decidedBy: decide_with_budget: cancellation and deadline first; an incomplete review waits for the owner; feasibility plus score_at_least accepts; otherwise the attempt and cost ceilings or plateau_attempts stop the run, else it retries.

options.label: Accept
options.say: Every required criterion passes and the score clears the threshold, so this exact draft becomes the champion.

options.label: Retry with feedback
options.say: Criteria are still unmet, so the better draft is kept or the old one restored, and the actor tries again with the critics' feedback.

options.label: Stop on plateau or budget
options.say: Attempts stopped improving, or the attempt, cost or time ceiling was reached, so nothing is accepted and the run stops.

options.label: Wait for the owner
options.say: The independent review came back unknown, so no improvement is credited and the run waits for the owner.

nodes.title: Owner answers the run
nodes.say: The owner's answer is recorded as fresh evidence against the exact pending request, the source epoch moves on, and the controller is relaunched to attempt again.

nodes.title: Route the accepted draft
nodes.say: Owner policy or a confident independent recommendation picks human review, automatic internal handoff or capture; anything uncertain defaults to human review.

nodes.title: Owner approves the handoff
nodes.say: On the human review route, the owner's Approve or Reject on that exact draft is recorded, and an approval lets the worker record the final handoff.

nodes.title: Result written to the task
nodes.say: The run's final report, checked against the execution's tool results unless the owner approved those exact bytes, becomes the task execution's outcome.

nodes.title: Browser primitive dispatch
nodes.say: The browser call is held to the agent's declared transport ceiling, then keyed to one cached session per execution, so open and click hit the same tab.

nodes.title: Session connects
nodes.say: On first use the session connects agent-browser to the magicutor CDP proxy, or opens a headed or headless browser when the mode asks for one.

nodes.title: agent-browser command
nodes.say: The dispatcher translates the tool call into agent-browser arguments and spawns one short-lived command-line process for this session.

nodes.title: Magicutor CDP proxy
nodes.say: Magicutor answers the DevTools WebSocket for this thread, and every browser command arrives as a Chrome DevTools Protocol message on that socket.

nodes.title: Tab ownership
nodes.say: Attach and close commands are checked against the tabs this execution owns, so an agent can only drive its own window and the popups it opened.

nodes.title: Bridge to Chrome
nodes.say: Allowed commands travel over the native bridge to the Chrome extension, which runs them through the debugger interface on the real tab.

nodes.title: Result returns
nodes.say: The command's output becomes the action's result; with API mining on, the network traces the proxy captured are drained and saved first.
